About.title: About Life Blackhole
About.lede: A quiet reminder that time is finite — so you use it. Not a prediction. Not a diagnosis.
About.numbersBody: Your estimate is the average remaining lifetime for people of your age, sex and country today, according to the United Nations. It describes a large group of people, not you. Your habits, health, luck and the decades of medical progress ahead all move your real number.
About.methodBody1: We look up remaining life expectancy at your current age from the UN's period life tables for {year}, interpolating between ages. Someone who is 30 has already survived childhood and youth, so their total is higher than life expectancy at birth.
About.methodBody2: The estimate is fixed for each year of your age and updated on your birthday, when your horizon moves back a little. If you've lived longer than your country's life expectancy at birth, we say so — every day after that is bonus time.
About.methodBody3: Without a country we use the world average; without a sex we use the combined table.
About.sourceBody: {citation} Abridged life tables, medium variant, {year}. {count, number} countries and areas plus the world average.
About.licenseNote: The 2024 download pages don't state a licence; earlier editions are published under CC BY 3.0 IGO. Credit to UN DESA.
About.statsBody: Weekends, full moons, heartbeats and the rest are rough illustrations using simple averages: about 70 heartbeats and 15 breaths a minute, a third of life asleep, one full moon every 29.5 days, one book a month. They're for perspective, not precision.
About.privacyBody: Your birth date and details are stored only in this browser. There's no account, no server and no tracking of personal data. Share images are made on your device, and your birth date is never on them unless you choose. You can delete everything in Settings at any time.
About.averageTitle: This is an average. You are not.
About.averageBody: Use it as a nudge, not a forecast.
